Topology object callbacks for banks, hash compare, funk, fec_sets, store, txncache, and exec_spad.

# Purpose
This file defines topology object callbacks for several runtime data structures used by the system. Each callback set provides the object `name`, the required memory `footprint`, the required memory `align`, and a `new` function that initializes the object in shared memory at the location returned by `fd_topo_obj_laddr`. The objects covered here are `banks`, `bh_cmp`, `funk`, `fec_sets`, `store`, `txncache`, and `exec_spad`, so the file acts as a registration point that connects topology configuration data to the constructors and size rules for these runtime components.

The code reads object parameters from the topology property set with `fd_pod_queryf_ulong` through the `VAL` macro. Those values control allocation sizes and limits such as `max_live_slots`, `max_fork_width`, `txn_max`, `rec_max`, `fec_max`, `part_cnt`, `max_txn_per_slot`, and `heap_max`. Some objects also use fixed alignment or fixed footprint helpers from other libraries, such as `fd_banks_*`, `fd_bank_hash_cmp_*`, `fd_funk_*`, `fd_store_*`, `fd_txncache_shmem_*`, and `fd_spad_*`. The `funk` object also handles seed selection, using a configured seed when present or generating one with `fd_rng_secure` when it is not.
